headline: High: Open Interpreter’s filesystem/code execution can collide with plano’s API-gateway role, creating default-path prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads/writes the local filesystem and clipboard by default, while plano consumes OpenAI-compatible chat/API inputs and can sit in the path of model traffic. If Open Interpreter’s outputs are copied into plano-managed prompts or configs, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not proven beyond docs.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter output is pasted into plano prompts or config files
IF plano forwards untrusted text into downstream model calls without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Use a separate scratch file for outputs and review before reuse
Add a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted text
Turn on manual approval for any prompt content imported from Open Interpreter
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem and broad network egress, while plano handles logs, traces, and metrics and exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If sensitive local files are fed into Open Interpreter and then forwarded through plano, data can leave the workstation. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter reads sensitive local files
IF plano logs or forwards those contents through its API path
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a non-sensitive directory
Redact secrets before sending text into plano
Disable verbose request/response logging in plano
Rotate any API keys exposed to Open Interpreter
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents onto separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has filesystem write and git-state modification, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem. Plano is an out-of-process dataplane with config-file input and broad network egress. If both touch the same repo or config tree, concurrent writes can overwrite each other. The overlap is real, but the profiles do not show unrestricted shared writes on both sides, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working directory
IF plano rewrites config.yaml while Open Interpreter edits repo files or git state
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
Make config.yaml read-only during Open Interpreter runs
Use file locks around shared mutable files
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code, shell commands, and file edits, and plano can act as an API gateway that may route or execute based on received text. If plano treats Open Interpreter output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or bad routing. The profiles do not prove automatic execution, so medium is the safer choice under uncertainty.
conditions: IF plano consumes Open Interpreter output without verification
IF generated commands or facts are used to update routing or automation
mitigations: Require human review before plano acts on Open Interpreter output
Add schema validation for any structured output
Compare outputs against a second source before execution
Log and diff all agent-produced instructions
requires-engineering: insert a verification step between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine, including secrets and local files, while plano’s documented data classes are logs, traces, and metrics. A compliance issue arises only if regulated local data is routed into plano’s logging or API path. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so this is a limited, conditional risk.
conditions: IF regulated local data is copied from Open Interpreter into plano logs or traces
IF the deployment requires retention or residency controls that plano does not enforce
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Open Interpreter sessions
Disable or minimize plano logging for sensitive runs
Use synthetic data for integration tests
Document a data-handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
